sources.title: EWAM: An Enhanced World Action Model for Closed-Loop Online Adaptation in Embodied Intelligence

synopsis: EWAM adds memory-conditioned generation, anomaly detection, discrete routing and action correction to a frozen Cosmos3-Nano--Policy-DROID policy. Its local advantage is execution efficiency: BananaInBowlTask time falls from 25.60 to 9.27 seconds while success stays at 100%. This adaptation uses accumulated simulation experience and lightweight updates, and increases inference latency. The evidence supports a bounded simulation deployment result, with unresolved figure and protocol inconsistencies. [e02, e10, e13, e15, e17]

problem.text: A plausible action can still collide, miss a grasp or waste motion when realized dynamics depart from predictions. EWAM asks whether a fixed pretrained WAM can exploit execution feedback without collecting another target-task demonstration dataset. Its zero-shot label permits memory growth and lightweight online learning.

contributions.text: Four trainable modules integrate retrieved experience and execution diagnostics into the frozen policy path; routing remains a supervised discrete decision.
A quality gate separates experience worth learning from diagnostic-only failures, while simulator rollback supplies recovery states.
The authors attribute local efficiency gains to memory-first adaptation and correction; the ablations support component sensitivity but do not separately establish the necessity of filtering.

inputs: Visual observation o_t, proprioceptive state q_t and language instruction l
Experience memory M and execution/contact diagnostics
outputs: Predicted next world state and raw action chunk
Corrected action chunk for environment execution; routing decision and qualified memory records

steps.name: Encode and generate
steps.detail: VLE encodes observation, proprioception and language; the AR reasoner produces context. The DiT generates a shared hidden representation used by frozen state and action heads. Robot tokens represent camera-pose delta, end-effector-pose delta and gripper state.

steps.name: Condition on admitted experience
steps.detail: At DiT layer 6, memory attention enters through a residual gate of 0.4 using five retrieved experiences. Proposed records store execution context, outcome and rollback anchor. The implemented compact backend is less rich than the full multimodal memory description.

steps.name: Diagnose and route
steps.detail: A six-component vector combines previous prediction error, candidate dynamics inconsistency and learned collision, empty-grasp, hallucination and force-risk scores. Routing combines this vector, AR context and memory. Reported operating regions are direct below 0.3, conservative from 0.3 to below 0.7, and rollback at or above 0.7.

steps.name: Execute, recover and admit
steps.detail: Direct routing keeps the raw action; conservative routing adds bounded correction; rollback restores a stable simulator checkpoint and replans. Without a stable state, recovery replans from the current state. Executed transitions are then filtered before memory writing or training.

training.text: Offline preparation combines action/state squared errors, memory cosine loss, binary risk and residual supervision, routing cross-entropy and anomaly-conditioned safe-action regression. Their weights are 1.0/0.5/0.3/0.8/0.6/1.2. Safe targets may come from simulator rollback, recovery primitives or admitted successful memory.

Only inserted layers and adapters receive updates; VLE, AR, DiT and output heads stay frozen. Online replay contains admitted samples only. Table 2 specifies learning rate 10^-4, rank-16 adapters and buffer size 1000; the exact update schedule and offline training corpus are unspecified.

inference.text: Retrieval affects the next generation without changing parameters. Realized next-state error is computed after execution; it is not an observation available for the current candidate. Section 3.4 supplies this causal ordering even though Eqs. (44)–(47) place a realized-error trigger before the transition.

Equation (52) requires SafetyScore≥0.75, TaskScore≥0.80, maximum gripper force≤0.80, EE SPARC≤−2.5, path≤1.2 m and time≤15 s. Rejected trajectories remain diagnostic-only. These are scenario-specific rules; the force quantity's units/normalization and SPARC computation are not fully specified.

equations.explanation: Observed state s and predicted state ŝ define two differently timed residuals: the previous residual is available when choosing an action; the realized residual follows execution.

Equation (25): a⁰ is the raw chunk, a* the executed corrected chunk, r the route, ι the anomaly vector and M memory. Correction strength α_corr is 0.5; the configured maximum joint correction is 0.3 rad.

Equation (51): θ denotes adaptable parameters, η learning rate, E an experience record, Q its quality gate, and U the scheduled-update indicator. Passing the gate enables learning but does not force an immediate update.

results.setting: RoboLab; same frozen backbone/interface; position σ=0.02 m and lighting ±15%; 5 seeds×25 trials; mean±95% CI.
results.interpretation: Reported time/path reductions are 63.8%/54.1%. Success is saturated; the finding concerns execution quality. Exact paired-test values are not supplied.

results.setting: Same local protocol; all seven displayed EWAM conditions have 100% success; Table 6 supplies point estimates.
results.value: Full 9.27 s; no self-learning 46.53 s; no correction 18.20 s; no memory 10.60 s; no rollback 10.27 s.
results.interpretation: Experience accumulation has the largest removal effect. Memory-only beating update-only does not establish update harm or a general ordering across tasks; the conditions change available mechanisms.

results.setting: 125 simulation evaluations per model; reported mean±95% CI.
results.interpretation: Preserved as reported: displayed category means sum to 1.7 and 11.0, respectively, not the total column. The missing accounting is unresolved.

results.setting: Same 5×25 protocol per task; three-task subset totals 375 evaluations per model; reported 95% CIs.
results.comparison: Baseline bin transfer: 100%, 18.40±1.85 s. Stacking: 87.2%±3.1%, 42.30±5.20 s.
results.interpretation: Stacking gains 7.2 percentage points of success. This extends evidence within the simulation subset, without isolating which recovery component causes the gain.

results.setting: Dual RTX 5880 Ada workstation, 48 GB/GPU; 100 inference trials; mean±SD.
results.comparison: Baseline 66.2±2.4 ms; 1690 MB: +15.4% latency and +7.7% memory.
results.interpretation: Faster task completion coexists with slower inference. The path exceeds a 20 Hz controller's 50 ms budget; buffered or asynchronous control is required for that target.

limitations.text: No physical-robot or sim-to-real result is reported. Recovery depends on simulator checkpoints, interfaces are backbone-specific, and compact memory remains vulnerable to occlusion, novel dynamics, ambiguous objects and long-horizon errors.

Figures 4 and 5 have swapped content/caption types. The ablation graphic says 20 episodes, while the tables describe 125 trials; the Figure 4 caption calls uncertainty both CI and SE. Table 6 point estimates are retained without inventing error bars.

Figure 1's module/update order does not match the formal loop. Figure 3 depicts a smoothness lower bound and force interval, whereas Eq. (52) specifies an EE SPARC upper bound and maximum force. Their equivalence is not established.
The filter's necessity is asserted from its design rather than isolated by a filter-disabled ablation. Capability comparisons with other named models are not matched empirical rankings.

reproduction.text: Preserve seeds 42/123/456/789/1024, deterministic matched trial order and memory reset per seed. Obtain the exact checkpoint, task/asset/simulator versions, module implementation, metric scripts and per-seed logs before attempting numerical replication.

Resolve offline data and training duration, initial memory contents, adapter reset policy, update cadence/minibatch size, action horizon/controller timing, dynamics-prior implementation and aggregate anomaly-score definition. The supplied specification does not determine these completely.

reasoning.text: The shared DiT representation feeds both state and action heads, supporting One Model at the backbone level; EWAM inserts memory into that path rather than merely co-training separate predictors. Its added mechanism is feedback routing, correction and filtered adaptation, consistent with Other mechanisms/Outside quadrants. Memory and policy post-training are supported; the stated objectives are supervised, so the combined WM-RL category should not be read as evidence of an RL algorithm.

discussionQuestions: Does the memory advantage arise on the first rollout or only after admitted experience accumulates? [e09, e11, e16]
Can filtering suppress harmful updates without starving the harder stacking task of useful experience? [e08, e14, e20]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author block, arXiv margin and abstract
evidence.detail: The title matches the catalog; credits are Xin Zhou (Astronex Robotics) and Cong Miao (Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology). The artifact is arXiv:2606.12690v1, 10 June 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–5, Sections 3.1–3.2, Eqs. (1)–(10)
evidence.detail: Visual observation, proprioception and language enter VLE and AR reasoning, followed by a memory-augmented DiT with shared-hidden-state state/action heads. Backbone parameters are frozen; inserted modules and adapters can change. Zero-shot excludes additional target-task demonstrations.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.3, Eqs. (11)–(14); p. 7, Table 2; p. 13, Section 3.11, Eqs. (53)–(56)
evidence.detail: Memory attention is injected residually at DiT layer 6; retrieval uses five items and gate 0.4. The proposed memory contains keys, execution values, outcomes and rollback anchors, with task/scene/layout/success retrieval weights 0.35/0.30/0.20/0.15.

Decision-time diagnostics use a previous residual, candidate dynamics inconsistency and four sigmoid risk heads. The realized residual is available after execution. Hallucination uses grasp confidence above 0.85 with force below 0.15 N. The later gated-system equations list a realized-error trigger before the transition.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Sections 3.5–3.6, Eqs. (22)–(26); p. 7, Table 2; p. 25, Appendix B, Table 10
evidence.detail: A supervised softmax/argmax router selects direct, conservative or rollback behavior. Reported anomaly regions are below 0.3, [0.3,0.7), and at least 0.7. Conservative correction has strength 0.5 and maximum joint correction 0.3 rad. Rollback uses simulator checkpoints, with current-state replanning if no stable state exists.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 10–11, Section 3.8, Eqs. (27)–(35), and Eq. (51); p. 7, Table 2; p. 24, Appendix A
evidence.detail: Training combines action, state, memory, anomaly, routing and correction losses with weights 1.0/0.5/0.3/0.8/0.6/1.2. Supervision can come from simulator labels and recovery targets. Online learning uses only admitted replay; learning rate is 10^-4, adapter rank 16, and buffer size 1000.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 8–10, Section 3.7 and Figure 2; p. 25, Appendix B
evidence.detail: The textual loop generates candidates, diagnoses and routes them, corrects and executes actions, then filters experience. Memory changes immediately upon admission and parameter updates are intermittent. Figure 2 depicts the post-execution anomaly/recovery and rejection branches.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Section 3.10, Eq. (52); p. 13, Figure 3
evidence.detail: All six conditions are required: SafetyScore at least 0.75, TaskScore at least 0.80, maximum gripper force at most 0.80, EE SPARC at most -2.5, path at most 1.2 m and time at most 15 s. Figure 3 instead depicts a generic smoothness lower bound and a force interval; no mapping to Eq. (52) is supplied.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 14–15, Sections 4.1, 4.4–4.5; p. 24, Appendix A and Table 9
evidence.detail: Matched RoboLab conditions use position perturbation sigma 0.02 m, lighting variation ±15%, and five named seeds with 25 trials each per task. Memory resets each seed; trial sequences match across models. The source reports mean ±1.96 SE and proposes paired seed-level tests.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Table 5 and Section 4.6; p. 14, Table 3
evidence.detail: BananaInBowlTask: both models have 100% success; baseline/EWAM time is 25.60±2.31/9.27±0.94 s, path 1.81±0.12/0.83±0.08 m, collisions 3.2±0.8/0.3±0.2, empty grasps 1.4±0.3/0.1±0.1, rollback 0/1.2±0.4. Table 5 labels intervals as 95% CIs; exact test values require logs.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 16–17, Section 4.7 and Table 6
evidence.detail: All seven displayed EWAM conditions reach 100% success. Full, no-memory, no-self-learning, no-correction, no-rollback, memory-only and update-only times are 9.27, 10.60, 46.53, 18.20, 10.27, 12.67 and 14.67 s; respective paths are 0.83, 0.95, 4.63, 1.42, 0.89, 0.99 and 1.07 m. Table 6 gives no intervals.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Section 4.8 and Table 7
evidence.detail: Reported total faults are 13.5±2.1 for the baseline and 2.2±0.6 for EWAM, with 95% CI labels. The four displayed category means are 3.2/1.4/2.1/4.3 and 0.3/0.1/0.4/0.9, which do not exhaust the stated totals; the difference is unexplained.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Section 4.3; p. 15, Table 4; p. 24, Table 9
evidence.detail: Latency over 100 trials is 66.2±2.4 ms baseline and 76.4±2.5 ms EWAM (mean±SD), with GPU memory 1690/1820 MB and throughput 621/520 step/s. The workstation has two RTX 5880 Ada GPUs, 48 GB each. The text acknowledges that 76.4 ms exceeds a 50 ms servo budget.

evidence.location: PDF p. 20, Table 8 and Section 4.9
evidence.detail: Three tasks yield 375 evaluations per model. BananasInBinOneMoreTask retains 100% success and reduces time from 18.40±1.85 to 11.20±1.12 s. BlockStackingOrderAgnosticTask changes success from 87.2%±3.1% to 94.4%±2.1%, time 42.30±5.20 to 28.60±3.10 s, and path 3.85±0.31 to 2.41±0.22 m; intervals are labeled 95% CIs.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 20–21, Sections 5–5.1; p. 26, Appendix C
evidence.detail: All validation is simulation-only, with limited tasks, layouts and backbone scope. Real-robot rollback is unvalidated; the compact memory does not implement the full proposed multimodal signatures. Occlusion, changed dynamics, object ambiguity, long horizons and sensor noise remain failure modes.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 24–25, Appendices A–B, Tables 9–10 and surrounding text
evidence.detail: Exact replication requires module code, task configurations, simulator/asset versions, checkpoint identity, metric scripts and per-seed logs. The source specifies deterministic sequences and memory resets, but does not fully specify offline data, update cadence, initialization, or all controller and model details.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Figure 4 image/caption; p. 19, Figure 5 image/caption; p. 17, Table 6
evidence.detail: Figure 4 contains qualitative failure panels although its caption describes quantitative ablations and calls error bars both 95% CIs and standard errors. Figure 5 contains the ablation bar chart although its caption describes qualitative failures. Its graphic says 20 episodes and has no visible uncertainty bars, unlike the main 125-trial protocol.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1 and Table 1; p. 25, Appendix C
evidence.detail: Other named VLA/WAM systems are compared at capability level, not under common measured protocols. The empirical control is the same frozen Cosmos3 policy interface without EWAM layers.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 1 and caption; pp. 4–5, Eqs. (1)–(10) and Section 3.2; p. 9, Section 3.7
evidence.detail: Figure 1 is a schematic with strategy selection before mismatch detection and self-learning before memory writing. The equations and textual loop instead specify anomaly detection before routing and qualified memory admission before scheduled updates; memory is inserted inside the DiT.

evidence.location: PDF p. 26, Table 11, filtering-necessity row; p. 17, Table 6; p. 12, Section 3.10
evidence.detail: The source calls filtering necessary, citing its design role. Table 6 does not include a filter-disabled comparison, so the empirical necessity of the six particular thresholds is not isolated.
